topic: What if Monkey D. Dragon never showed up at Loguetown and Smoker actually succeeded in arresting Luffy, forcing Garp to personally intervene instead
title: What If Luffy Was Captured At Loguetown?
description:
The wiki says it plainly: Smoker would have successfully arrested Luffy at Loguetown if Dragon hadn't interfered. This is the chapter-cited What If where that interference never happens, Luffy's own crew fails its first rescue attempt, and Garp has to personally pull rank on Smoker to set his grandson free.

Following the story's own rules for Garp, Smoker, and the crew, this traces exactly how different Smoker's entire rivalry with Luffy becomes when a grudge replaces a mystery.
comment: If Garp had to personally free Luffy at Loguetown instead of Dragon, does Smoker's whole rivalry with Luffy change for good?

lines.text: Three separate things had to go right for Luffy to ever reach the Grand Line out of Loguetown.

shot.search: Luffy Loguetown three things go right
shot.fallback: young pirate standing on the edge of a decisive town

lines.text: A lightning bolt. A cannonball. And one Revolutionary who happened to be walking through town that day.

shot.search: Lightning cannonball Revolutionary Loguetown clues
shot.fallback: three separate strokes of fortune lining up at once

lines.text: So what actually happens if that third one, Monkey D. Dragon, simply never shows up at all?

shot.search: Dragon never shows question Loguetown
shot.fallback: absent savior leaving a desperate moment unresolved

lines.text: Smoker already had Luffy pinned to the ground, cuffed, with every intention of finishing the arrest.

shot.search: Smoker pins Luffy cuffed arrest Loguetown
shot.fallback: captain pinning down a cornered young pirate

lines.text: The wiki says it outright: Smoker would have succeeded, if Dragon hadn't interfered...

shot.search: Smoker would succeed without Dragon wiki
shot.fallback: nearly successful capture cut short by one arrival

lines.text: Take that one arrival away, and the entire story bends in a direction nobody saw coming...

shot.search: Take away arrival story bends direction
shot.fallback: single missing arrival reshaping an entire future

lines.text: This isn't a random, out-of-nowhere change either. It's removing exactly one documented event the wiki itself confirms happened.

shot.search: Not random removing one documented event
shot.fallback: a single, specific fact lifted straight from the record

lines.text: Everything that follows still uses the same characters, the same motives, and the same rules the actual story already set up.

shot.search: Same characters motives rules story setup
shot.fallback: familiar rules governing an unfamiliar outcome

lines.text: Picture the real version first. A storm breaks over Loguetown as Smoker corners Luffy in the town square.

shot.search: Storm breaks Smoker corners Luffy square
shot.fallback: sudden storm rolling over a tense standoff

lines.text: Dragon happens to be walking through that exact street, watching his own son about to be taken.

shot.search: Dragon walks street watches son Loguetown
shot.fallback: quiet figure watching a desperate confrontation unfold

lines.text: A massive gust of wind, likely Dragon's own doing, blows the Marines back and frees Luffy on the spot.

shot.search: Gust wind blows Marines frees Luffy
shot.fallback: powerful gust scattering an entire Marine unit

lines.text: Now take that one moment out entirely. Dragon is delayed somewhere else, or simply never walks down that street at all.

shot.search: Dragon delayed never walks street removed
shot.fallback: single absent figure changing an entire outcome

lines.text: Smoker finishes the arrest exactly the way he intended to, Seastone cuffs locked tight around both of Luffy's wrists.

shot.search: Smoker finishes arrest Seastone cuffs locked
shot.fallback: successful capture finally completed without interference

lines.text: For the first time in his short career, Luffy is actually, fully in Marine custody, with no storm left to save him.

shot.search: Luffy fully Marine custody no storm
shot.fallback: captured pirate with no last-minute rescue in sight

lines.text: Smoker radios ahead immediately, requesting transport to the nearest Marine base before anyone can organize a rescue.

shot.search: Smoker radios transport nearest Marine base
shot.fallback: urgent call securing a hard-won capture

lines.text: A teenage Marine recruit named Koby watches the entire thing happen, stunned that the pirate he once admired actually lost...

shot.search: Koby watches stunned Luffy actually lost
shot.fallback: young recruit watching a hero's streak finally break

lines.text: Zoro, Nami, Usopp, and Sanji are all already part of the crew by this point in the story.

shot.search: Zoro Nami Usopp Sanji crew Loguetown
shot.fallback: four loyal crewmates standing ready to fight back

lines.text: Nami actually argues against rushing in blind, pointing out that Marine garrisons at Loguetown are famously well stocked for exactly this kind of attack.

shot.search: Nami argues against rushing in blind
shot.fallback: cautious navigator pushing back on a reckless plan

lines.text: Usopp is openly terrified too, but nobody on that crew seriously considers leaving their captain behind, not even for a second.

shot.search: Usopp terrified nobody considers leaving captain
shot.fallback: fearful crewmate standing firm despite the danger

lines.text: They regroup fast and storm the Marine post, trying to pull Luffy out before transport ever arrives.

shot.search: Crew storms Marine post before transport
shot.fallback: desperate crew charging a heavily guarded outpost

lines.text: Loguetown isn't some sleepy outpost, though. It's the town built around Gol D. Roger's own final stand, heavily garrisoned for exactly this reason.

shot.search: Loguetown heavily garrisoned Roger scaffold town
shot.fallback: fortified town built around a legendary old scaffold

lines.text: Smoker's Logia body alone makes most direct attacks on him pointless, and his officer Tashigi backs him at every turn.

shot.search: Smoker Logia Tashigi backs every turn
shot.fallback: intangible officer supported by a loyal second

lines.text: Zoro trades blows with Smoker directly and barely slows him down, same as he barely managed in the story everyone actually knows.

shot.search: Zoro trades blows Smoker barely slows
shot.fallback: skilled swordsman unable to land a lasting blow

lines.text: The crew gets pushed back hard, forced to retreat toward their ship without Luffy anywhere in sight.

shot.search: Crew pushed back retreat without Luffy
shot.fallback: desperate retreat leaving their captain behind

lines.text: Zoro takes that failure the hardest of anyone. He already carries a vow never to lose again after Mihawk, and this feels exactly like that.

shot.search: Zoro hardest personal vow never lose again
shot.fallback: proud swordsman furious at failing his own standard

lines.text: He wants to go straight back in alone. Nami physically stops him, pointing out that one more reckless attempt gets him captured too.

shot.search: Zoro wants back alone Nami stops him
shot.fallback: hotheaded swordsman reined in by a cooler head

lines.text: Sanji takes the fight the most personally of all, furious that his brand new captain got taken before they'd even reached the Grand Line properly.

shot.search: Sanji furious captain taken Grand Line
shot.fallback: newly recruited cook burning with fresh loyalty

lines.text: Even Luffy himself, cuffed and dragged through town, keeps shouting for his crew to run instead of risking themselves on his behalf.

shot.search: Luffy shouts crew run instead risking
shot.fallback: cornered captain more worried for his crew than himself

lines.text: Nobody listens to him, obviously. That's never once worked on this crew, and it doesn't work here either.

shot.search: Nobody listens never works this crew
shot.fallback: loyal crew ignoring an order they never intended to follow

lines.text: That's the first real cost of this change: the crew's very first rescue attempt, and it fails completely.

shot.search: First rescue attempt fails completely cost
shot.fallback: a crew's first real test ending in failure

lines.text: Smoker doesn't gloat about beating them either. He's far too focused on getting Luffy processed before anything else can go wrong.

shot.search: Smoker focused processing not gloating
shot.fallback: disciplined officer prioritizing the mission over pride

lines.text: A capture this clean, on the exact spot Gol D. Roger once stood, is the kind of story that makes careers inside the Marines.

shot.search: Capture clean Roger spot makes careers
shot.fallback: historic capture carrying real weight for a Marine career

lines.text: Smoker already has a reputation for ignoring other notable pirates once he's locked onto a target, and right now that target is secured.

shot.search: Smoker ignores pirates locked onto target
shot.fallback: singular focus blocking out every other distraction

lines.text: Word of the failed rescue spreads fast anyway, reaching exactly the one Marine who always handles Luffy personally...

shot.search: Word spreads reaches Marine handles personally
shot.fallback: news traveling fast toward one particular Marine

lines.text: That Marine is Monkey D. Garp, and he has a long, established habit of handling his grandson's messes himself.

shot.search: Garp long habit handling grandson messes
shot.fallback: legendary Marine already bracing for family trouble

lines.text: Garp already refused to capture Luffy once before at Water 7, until he was explicitly ordered to do so.

shot.search: Garp refused capture Luffy Water 7 ordered
shot.fallback: reluctant Marine previously resisting an official order

lines.text: He consistently bends Marine rules around his own family, valuing them over his actual duty again and again.

shot.search: Garp bends rules family over duty
shot.fallback: repeated pattern of family outweighing official duty

lines.text: Even Roger himself once said he and Garp nearly ended each other many times, across years of mutual, almost respectful pursuit.

shot.search: Roger Garp nearly end each other years
shot.fallback: two legendary rivals locked in a respectful, decades-long chase

lines.text: That history of mutual respect for a pirate is exactly the kind of thing that makes Garp so unpredictable to officers like Smoker.

shot.search: History respect pirate unpredictable officers Smoker
shot.fallback: unconventional respect baffling officers raised on stricter rules

lines.text: Garp has also turned down every single offer to become an Admiral, specifically because he refuses to answer to the Celestial Dragons.

shot.search: Garp refuses Admiral Celestial Dragons answer
shot.fallback: principled refusal turning down an ordinary man's dream promotion

lines.text: That's a man who already treats rank as something to use selectively, not something to chase for its own sake.

shot.search: Garp treats rank selectively not chase
shot.fallback: selective use of power, never pursued for its own sake

lines.text: Once word reaches him through the ranks that Luffy is actually, fully in custody, Garp doesn't wait for permission to act.

shot.search: Garp does not wait permission acts
shot.fallback: legendary Marine moving before anyone can stop him

lines.text: Hearing that Smoker actually succeeded where Garp usually intervenes first, Garp personally travels to Loguetown to handle it himself.

shot.search: Garp travels Loguetown handle himself personally
shot.fallback: legendary Marine arriving to settle things in person

lines.text: As a Vice Admiral, Garp easily outranks Smoker, and simply overrides the custody arrangement on the spot.

shot.search: Garp outranks Smoker overrides custody spot
shot.fallback: overwhelming rank settling the matter instantly

lines.text: He drags Luffy aside, delivers the exact same bone-headed Fist of Love lecture he always gives him, and lets him go.

shot.search: Garp lectures Fist of Love lets go
shot.fallback: familiar family lecture ending in a quiet release

lines.text: In front of his own men, Smoker watches his hard-earned catch simply walk free, with zero explanation given to him at all.

shot.search: Smoker watches catch walk free no explanation
shot.fallback: humiliating loss witnessed by an entire garrison

lines.text: Garp doesn't even bother explaining his reasoning to Smoker at all. He simply states that the matter is now handled, and walks away.

shot.search: Garp states matter handled walks away
shot.fallback: dismissive authority offering no explanation at all

lines.text: Tashigi tries defending her captain's actions, pointing out the arrest was entirely legitimate under every Marine rule that applies.

shot.search: Tashigi defends Smoker arrest legitimate rules
shot.fallback: loyal officer defending a decision nobody asked her to

lines.text: Garp doesn't argue the point. He simply outranks the entire conversation and leaves with Luffy regardless.

shot.search: Garp outranks conversation leaves regardless
shot.fallback: overwhelming rank ending a debate before it starts

lines.text: Smoker still files an official report anyway, documenting every single detail of a by-the-book arrest that still somehow slipped through his own fingers.

shot.search: Smoker files report arrest slipped fingers
shot.fallback: meticulous paperwork recording a frustrating, unjust loss

lines.text: Nobody above him ever even reads it closely at all. Garp's own towering reputation alone makes the whole incident quietly disappear from the official record.

shot.search: Nobody reads report Garp reputation disappears
shot.fallback: quiet erasure protecting a legend's casual intervention

lines.text: That humiliation doesn't just sting for a day. It reshapes exactly how Smoker thinks about Luffy from this point forward...

shot.search: Humiliation reshapes Smoker thinks Luffy forward
shot.fallback: lasting resentment beginning to take root

lines.text: In the real story, Smoker's whole obsession with Luffy starts as a mystery: why would a Revolutionary save a random pirate?

shot.search: Real story Smoker mystery Dragon saves
shot.fallback: original fascination built on an unanswered question

lines.text: In this version, there's no mystery left to chase at all. Smoker knows exactly what happened: Garp's favoritism cost him his arrest.

shot.search: No mystery Smoker knows Garp favoritism
shot.fallback: plain explanation replacing an old fascination

lines.text: Smoker already holds grudges against pirates who escape him. This time, his grudge points at a fellow Marine instead.

shot.search: Smoker grudge points fellow Marine instead
shot.fallback: familiar resentment redirected toward his own side

lines.text: He's genuinely good at his job too. Pirate activity around Loguetown had already dropped sharply the moment Smoker first took charge of the post.

shot.search: Smoker good job pirate activity dropped
shot.fallback: competent officer whose record now carries an asterisk

lines.text: That competence is exactly why this particular loss stings so much worse than an ordinary escaped pirate ever would.

shot.search: Competence why loss stings worse ordinary
shot.fallback: a skilled officer's rare failure cutting deeper than most

lines.text: Losing a clean, by-the-book arrest to a superior's personal favoritism cuts directly against everything Smoker actually values about his own work.

shot.search: Losing arrest favoritism cuts Smoker values
shot.fallback: painful contradiction striking at his core professional identity

lines.text: Tashigi notices the change in him almost immediately, describing him as colder and far less willing to explain his decisions afterward.

shot.search: Tashigi notices Smoker colder less willing
shot.fallback: loyal officer watching her captain grow more distant

lines.text: She still follows him anyway, same as always, even without fully understanding what actually changed in him that day.

shot.search: Tashigi follows anyway not understanding change
shot.fallback: unwavering loyalty continuing despite an unexplained shift

lines.text: Loyalty like that doesn't really ask too many questions at all. It just quietly stays, and that's exactly enough for Smoker right now.

shot.search: Loyalty stays enough for Smoker now
shot.fallback: quiet loyalty asking nothing in return, and needing nothing explained

lines.text: He requests a transfer deeper into the Grand Line anyway, chasing Luffy with the exact same intensity as before.

shot.search: Smoker requests transfer chases Luffy intensity
shot.fallback: unchanged determination despite a very different motive

lines.text: The difference is what's fueling it now: not awe at a mysterious parallel to Gol D. Roger, but plain resentment at being overruled.

shot.search: Difference fueling resentment overruled not awe
shot.fallback: bitter resentment replacing an old sense of wonder

lines.text: That's one unbreakable rule of a good What If: change one event, and the motive underneath everything else shifts with it...

shot.search: Rule What If motive shifts underneath
shot.fallback: single change rippling through an entire character's motive

lines.text: Years later, at Arabasta, the real story has Smoker siding with Luffy against Crocodile, out of a shared sense of justice.

shot.search: Real story Smoker sides Luffy Arabasta
shot.fallback: unlikely alliance forming around a shared enemy

lines.text: In this version, that alliance still happens, because Crocodile's crimes against Arabasta are exactly as real either way.

shot.search: Alliance still happens Crocodile crimes real
shot.fallback: same crisis demanding the same uneasy cooperation

lines.text: What's different is what Smoker is actually thinking while he fights alongside Luffy instead of against him.

shot.search: Different what Smoker thinking fighting alongside
shot.fallback: identical teamwork hiding a very different inner monologue

lines.text: In the real story, Smoker respects Luffy's conviction. Here, Smoker is still quietly resentful of the entire Monkey D. family's special treatment.

shot.search: Smoker resentful Monkey D family treatment
shot.fallback: grudging cooperation masking an unresolved personal resentment

lines.text: He still does the right thing at Arabasta. He just does it with far less faith in the system he actually serves.

shot.search: Still right thing less faith system
shot.fallback: right outcome reached through a far more cynical path

lines.text: Smoker still personally witnesses Luffy declare his dream to become Pirate King out loud, same as he does in the original story.

shot.search: Smoker witnesses Luffy declare dream Pirate King
shot.fallback: familiar declaration landing on an officer who still remembers the day he lost him

lines.text: That declaration lands differently on a man nursing a grudge than it does on a man still chasing an unanswered mystery.

shot.search: Declaration lands differently grudge versus mystery
shot.fallback: same words striking very different emotional nerves

lines.text: Later, during the chaos at Punk Hazard, Smoker and Luffy end up allies again too, forced together by a far bigger threat.

shot.search: Smoker Luffy allies Punk Hazard again
shot.fallback: two reluctant allies forced together once more

lines.text: That alliance still works exactly the same way it always did: not friendship, just two people who happen to want the same outcome.

shot.search: Alliance works same way not friendship
shot.fallback: functional cooperation that never quite becomes real trust

lines.text: That's the quiet difference a single changed afternoon in Loguetown leaves behind, years later and oceans away...

shot.search: Quiet difference changed afternoon years later
shot.fallback: small change still echoing years after the fact

lines.text: There's a quieter cost buried inside all of this, one that has nothing to do with Smoker at all.

shot.search: Quieter cost nothing to do Smoker
shot.fallback: overlooked loss hiding beneath the obvious one

lines.text: In the real story, Dragon gets to watch his son sail off toward the Grand Line, even from a distance.

shot.search: Dragon watches son sail Grand Line distance
shot.fallback: distant father quietly watching a son's departure

lines.text: In this version, Dragon never gets that moment either. He's simply absent, somewhere else entirely, missing it completely.

shot.search: Dragon absent missing moment entirely version
shot.fallback: absent father missing the one moment that mattered

lines.text: Luffy still has no idea who his father even is at this point in the story, same as always.

shot.search: Luffy no idea father same always
shot.fallback: unaware son with no clue about his own lineage

lines.text: But in the real version, Garp at least knows Dragon was there, watching, even if Luffy never finds out.

shot.search: Garp knows Dragon watching Luffy unaware
shot.fallback: quiet knowledge known to only one witness

lines.text: Here, Garp doesn't get that small comfort either. As far as he knows, his son wasn't even in Loguetown that day.

shot.search: Garp no comfort son not Loguetown
shot.fallback: missing reassurance leaving an old worry unresolved

lines.text: Garp already disapproves of Dragon's entire path as a Revolutionary, same as he disapproves of Luffy choosing piracy over the Marines.

shot.search: Garp disapproves Dragon Revolutionary path same
shot.fallback: disappointed father figure facing two rebellious paths

lines.text: Without even that small, secondhand proof that Dragon still quietly watches over his own son, Garp's worry only grows heavier.

shot.search: Without proof Dragon watches Garp worry grows
shot.fallback: unresolved worry compounding without any reassurance at all

lines.text: Sengoku still reveals Dragon's identity publicly at Marineford years later either way, since that reveal never depended on Loguetown at all.

shot.search: Sengoku reveals Dragon Marineford either way
shot.fallback: unchanged revelation arriving through its own separate path

lines.text: Young Coby, still processing what he just watched, comes away from Loguetown with a very different first lesson about the Marines.

shot.search: Coby different first lesson about Marines
shot.fallback: impressionable recruit drawing a harder lesson than expected

lines.text: In the real story, Coby sees Dragon's quiet act of love and grows up believing in justice tempered by mercy.

shot.search: Real story Coby sees mercy grows justice
shot.fallback: idealistic lesson shaping a young recruit's entire worldview

lines.text: Here, all he actually sees is one powerful man overruling another, which quietly teaches him that rank decides everything, not justice.

shot.search: Coby sees rank decides not justice
shot.fallback: cynical lesson about power replacing an idealistic one

lines.text: That's a small, easy-to-miss change with a long reach: the exact same boy, shaped by a slightly colder lesson.

shot.search: Small change long reach same boy
shot.fallback: a single afternoon quietly reshaping a future Marine

lines.text: Years later, that same Coby still ends up pleading for both sides to stop fighting at Marineford, same as always.

shot.search: Coby pleads stop fighting Marineford same
shot.fallback: idealistic young Marine still begging for peace years later

lines.text: The plea just comes from someone who learned justice is complicated a few years earlier than he otherwise would have...

shot.search: Plea complicated justice earlier than otherwise
shot.fallback: the same hard-won wisdom, arriving just a little sooner

lines.text: One missing man changes what three different people quietly believe about where they stand with each other...

shot.search: One missing man changes three people
shot.fallback: single absence rippling through three separate relationships

lines.text: So here's how the one change plays out: Luffy still reaches the Grand Line, just through Garp's favor instead of Dragon's wind.

shot.search: Luffy reaches Grand Line Garp favor
shot.fallback: same destination reached through a very different door

lines.text: His crew learns a harder lesson early: pride alone doesn't win a rescue against a well-defended Marine town.

shot.search: Crew learns lesson pride alone rescue
shot.fallback: humbling lesson learned before the real voyage even starts

lines.text: Smoker becomes just as obsessed with chasing Luffy as he ever was, but for a bitterer, far more personal reason this time around.

shot.search: Smoker obsessed bitterer personal reason time
shot.fallback: same obsession, driven by a far colder motive

lines.text: Garp, for his own part, never once thinks of any of this as a big deal at all. To him, it's just another ordinary mess from his grandson.

shot.search: Garp never big deal just another mess
shot.fallback: legendary Marine treating a huge moment as routine

lines.text: That mismatch, Garp's total indifference against Smoker's genuine humiliation, is exactly why the grudge sticks so hard in the first place.

shot.search: Mismatch indifference humiliation grudge sticks
shot.fallback: lopsided reaction explaining why one side never lets go

lines.text: A legend who barely notices the damage he causes, and a dedicated officer stuck carrying every bit of it afterward.

shot.search: Legend barely notices officer carries damage
shot.fallback: uneven weight settling on the one person who actually felt it

lines.text: Some fans will say this barely changes anything, since Luffy still ends up free and still reaches the Grand Line regardless.

shot.search: Fans say barely changes Luffy free regardless
shot.fallback: fair point questioning how much actually shifted

lines.text: That's a fair point on the surface. The destination doesn't change. Who Luffy owes that freedom to absolutely does.

shot.search: Fair point destination same who owes differs
shot.fallback: surface outcome unchanged, underlying debt completely different

lines.text: And it's worth saying plainly: Luffy himself comes out of this completely unaware anything was ever even different at all.

shot.search: Luffy unaware anything different plainly stated
shot.fallback: oblivious captain untouched by a change he never noticed

lines.text: He still sets sail with the exact same confidence, the exact same dream, and the exact same crew standing behind him.

shot.search: Luffy sets sail same confidence crew
shot.fallback: unchanged hero sailing forward, oblivious to what shifted

lines.text: That's actually the most unsettling part of this whole exercise: the hero of the story never even notices how close the ending nearly went wrong.

shot.search: Unsettling hero never notices close call
shot.fallback: unaware protagonist blissfully ignorant of how close disaster came

lines.text: Every single consequence in this story lands on the people around Luffy, never on Luffy himself.

shot.search: Consequences land people around not Luffy
shot.fallback: ripple effects absorbed entirely by everyone else around him

lines.text: In the real story, Garp also knows Dragon was there watching. That knowledge quietly softens how Garp handles everything that comes after.

shot.search: Garp knowledge Dragon softens handling after
shot.fallback: quiet reassurance shaping how a grandfather lets go

lines.text: Strip that reassurance away, and every future choice Garp makes about Luffy carries just a little more fear in it.

shot.search: Strip reassurance future choice more fear
shot.fallback: missing comfort adding weight to every future decision

lines.text: Owing your freedom to a father who loves you from a distance is different from owing it to a grandfather who outranks the man holding you.

shot.search: Owing freedom father versus grandfather different
shot.fallback: two very different debts shaping two very different futures

lines.text: One is a quiet act of love. The other is a Marine simply pulling rank on another Marine in front of his own men.

shot.search: One quiet love other pulling rank
shot.fallback: tender gesture contrasted against a cold display of power

lines.text: Both versions still end with Luffy free and sailing off toward the Grand Line. Only one of them leaves a lasting scar behind on someone else.

shot.search: Both versions free sailing lasting scar
shot.fallback: identical outcome for Luffy, very different cost for everyone around him

lines.text: Smoker spends the rest of his career chasing a grudge instead of chasing a mystery, and that changes the shape of every fight after this one.

shot.search: Smoker chases grudge instead mystery career
shot.fallback: altered motive reshaping an entire career's worth of rivalry

lines.text: Change one storm, one wind, one absent father, and the whole story still arrives in the same place, carrying a very different weight.

shot.search: Change one storm arrives weight different
shot.fallback: familiar destination reached by carrying a very different burden

lines.text: That's the actual value of asking this kind of question in the first place: not to rewrite the ending, but to see what it actually costs.

shot.search: Value asking question not rewrite costs
shot.fallback: the real point of the exercise laid out plainly

lines.text: Luffy's story barely blinks. Everyone standing just outside the frame pays the real price for that one missing afternoon.

shot.search: Luffy barely blinks everyone pays price
shot.fallback: a protagonist's smooth path built on someone else's cost

lines.text: And if you want to see what happens the day Smoker finally learns the real reason Dragon was never actually there, that's the next story.

shot.search: Smoker learns real reason Dragon next story
shot.fallback: unresolved truth waiting to surface in a future story
